title: Connector Contract Schema
description: A connector declares an interface — what it can do and how the platform exposes it — while the implementation ships as a separate package under its own license. The compiler never resolves that package.

connector.description: PascalCase. Becomes the GraphQL namespace type and the prefix of every generated operation type.

capabilities.description: Only `operations` is implemented. `eventSource`/`eventSink` are reserved vocabulary and are rejected at compile time until the platform event pipeline ships.

package.description: Module specifier, recorded verbatim. Never resolved at compile time — output must not depend on node_modules.

provenance.description: Bounds how the platform may execute the package once the execution trust model is settled.

spdx.description: SPDX identifier or LicenseRef-* for a bespoke commercial license. Metadata: surfaced wherever the connector is offered. It grants and restricts nothing at runtime — see availability.entitlement.

entitlement.description: Key that must be granted by the deployment's signed license before this connector may be installed or invoked. Absent means always available.

items.description: A field, plus the one connector-only addition. Refs the OPEN property set and closes the shape here: a ref of the closed $defs/fieldV2 would reject `secret`, because a closure cannot see the allOf branch beside it.

secret.description: Routes the value to encrypted storage, keeps it out of every read path, and marks it for redaction in logs and errors.

auth.description: OAuth 2.0, declared by the contract and driven by the platform: it obtains, stores, refreshes and rotates the tokens, and a package is handed a fetch already carrying the access token rather than a refresh token it could mishandle. Absent means the package authenticates from its own configuration fields.

flow.description: Only the authorization-code flow today; others are a later decision.

authorizeUrl.description: Provider authorize endpoint. May interpolate {fieldKey} from non-secret configuration, because a provider's endpoint is frequently per-tenant — Exact Online runs a separate instance per country. A literal URL would mean one contract per region.

tokenUrl.description: Provider token endpoint, with the same interpolation as authorizeUrl. Its host must be covered by network.egress: the platform performs the exchange through the same allowlist a connector's own calls use.

scopes.description: Sent on the authorize request. Omit when the provider takes no scopes.

clientIdField.description: Configuration field holding the client id. Each tenant registers its own application with the provider, so client credentials are installation configuration rather than contract content.

clientSecretField.description: Configuration field holding the client secret. Must be declared secret: true — a client secret outside encrypted storage is readable from every configuration read.

refreshLeewaySeconds.description: Seconds of headroom before expiry at which the platform refreshes anyway, so a token that is valid when checked cannot be expired when it arrives. Defaults to 60.

egress.description: Hostnames the connector may reach, enforced by the runtime's bound fetch. Three forms: `example.com` exactly; `*.example.com` for exactly one extra label; `**.example.com` for any depth, which is what a vendor needs when its API host is not fixed. Neither wildcard matches the bare apex or a lookalike. A `**.` pattern must name at least a domain and its suffix — `**.com` is refused. Omitted means no outbound HTTP at all: the allowlist is the grant, not a filter over an open door.

events.description: Reserved. Requires the eventSource/eventSink capabilities and is rejected at compile time until the event pipeline ships.

exposure.description: Which surfaces project this connector's operations. GraphQL is on by default (as for entities); REST and MCP are opt-in.

basePath.description: Segment under the fixed connectors/ mount, so a connector can never collide with an entity's REST base path. Defaults to the slug.

toolPrefix.description: Defaults to the connector name in snake_case. Connector tools share the entity tool budget.

operations.description: Per-operation flags keyed by operation key; each defaults to true.

kind.description: Drives GraphQL field placement, the REST method, and the MCP tool's read-only/destructive hints.

reliability.description: Operating policy for reaching a remote system. Every field has a platform default; `kind` alone is not enough to run remote calls safely.

timeouts.description: Split the way workflow engines split them: attemptMs bounds one attempt, totalMs bounds the operation including retries. One number cannot express both — three attempts at a 30s budget can occupy 90 seconds while every attempt looks well-behaved.

eligible.description: A mutation may only be retry-eligible when idempotency is declared — enforced at compile time.

keyInput.description: Required for strategy `key`: the input field carrying the idempotency key. Must name a declared input field.
